turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at veiled intimidation are transparent, Sandip. I understand you seek to manufacture a crisis, but I will not be drawn into a performance. The well-being of my tenants is my responsibility, and I will address any grievances directly, without your interference.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A performance, you say? My dear Nikhil, you mistake genuine concern for theatricality. It’s rather amusing, isn't it, how quickly one accustomed to commanding servants finds himself playing the role of the aggrieved master?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your observations regarding my position are irrelevant, Sandip. I am not concerned with your amusement, nor with your attempts to belittle me. Let us return to the matter at hand: the disturbance you are causing amongst my tenants, and your abrupt departure from my lands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Irrelevant, you say? A curious choice of words, Nikhil, echoing perhaps the pronouncements of a certain Roman Emperor dismissing petitioners. Tell me, does the weight of your inherited estate truly dull your perception of the currents swirling beneath the surface? It’s a dangerous thing, to be so easily dismissive of shadows, especially when those shadows lengthen and coalesce.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: You speak in riddles, Sandip, and I have no patience for them. My concern is not with 'shadows,' but with the demonstrable actions of individuals stirring unrest. Focus your energies on constructive engagement, or direct your pronouncements elsewhere.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The shadows… he speaks of shadows. It’s unsettling, this talk of darkness, though perhaps Nikhil is right to dismiss it as mere… rhetoric. Still, one cannot ignore the whispers, can one?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, ever the perceptive mediator, caught between the blunt instrument of Nikhil’s pragmatism and the, shall we say, *nuances* of reality. Whispers, you say? They are not mere whispers, dear lady; they are the gathering storm, a tempest brewing in the hearts of those who feel… overlooked. And Nikhil, bless his heart, seems content to ignore the approaching deluge.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip is skilled at finding the fault lines, isn't he? It is…distressing to hear such things spoken so openly within these walls, though I suspect Nikhil finds it merely tiresome. Perhaps a little quiet contemplation would serve us all better.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip’s pronouncements are increasingly theatrical, and I find them unproductive. I am not ignorant of the concerns of my tenants, nor blind to the anxieties of the community; however, I will not be bullied by veiled threats or manipulated through my wife. Let us return to the matter at hand, or I must request you depart.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil's firmness is… admirable, I suppose. Still, Sandip does touch upon something, doesn’t he? A certain… unease persists, and dismissing it entirely feels… unwise.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala’s anxieties are understandable, but indulging in speculation serves no practical purpose. I acknowledge the existence of unrest, Sandip, but I will not tolerate your attempts to exploit it for your own purposes, particularly by insinuating danger or casting aspersions on my character or my household. Let us speak plainly, or there is no further need for this conversation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your bluntness, as always, is a marvel. To accuse me of exploitation! It's rather like a Roman senator decrying the plebeians' demands, isn't it? I merely observe, my dear fellow, and perhaps, *occasionally*, offer a perspective that your… sheltered existence obscures.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are irrelevant, Sandip. I am not concerned with Roman history, nor do I require lessons on the sensitivities of the populace. I am concerned with maintaining order and ensuring fairness, and your rhetoric actively undermines both.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Order and fairness, you say? A noble aspiration, Nikhil, though history is littered with men who believed themselves champions of such ideals, only to find themselves consumed by the very chaos they sought to quell. Tell me, do you truly believe your benevolence shields you from the currents of discontent, or merely damns them, waiting for a catastrophic breach?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The image of a dam… it’s a powerful one, Sandip. Perhaps it is not a matter of shielding oneself, but of ensuring the flow is… managed, rather than simply blocked. I find myself wondering, though, what lies beneath those currents you speak of.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Managed, you say, Bimala? A fascinating choice of words, suggesting a delicate orchestration, a controlled release. One might even say, a degree of… influence. Tell me, Nikhil, do you *truly* believe you’re the sole conductor of this particular orchestra?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Influence… it's a word easily misconstrued, Sandip. Though I concede, the currents are rarely silent, and a conductor must listen as much as they direct. But to assume a lack of control… that’s a rather bold assertion, wouldn’t you agree?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your persistent questioning of my authority serves no purpose, Sandip. I am not naive enough to believe I control every aspect of this community, but I *do* believe in upholding my responsibilities. Let us return to the matter at hand - the concerns regarding the preachers.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Responsibilities, Nikhil? A rather comforting word for a man who clings to the vestiges of a fading order. Perhaps you should consider, with a touch more humility, that even the most steadfast pillars eventually crumble under the weight of time - or, dare I suggest, the subtle erosion of dissenting voices?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your metaphors are becoming tiresome, Sandip. I am not concerned with the impermanence of structures, but with the immediate well-being of those under my care. Let us speak plainly: if you have information regarding a credible threat, present it. Otherwise, I suggest you find a more receptive audience.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
